# PX4/NuttX Firmware Workspace

Repository-local backend: `Tools/firmware-workspace.py`. Extension: `Tools/vscode_extension/`.
Read `docs/vscode-extension.md` for installation, native views, host limits and safety boundaries.
Use the checked-out schemas as the contract; do not invent target catalogs or loader recipes.

## CLI

```bash
python3 Tools/firmware-workspace.py catalog --json
python3 Tools/firmware-workspace.py doctor --json
python3 Tools/firmware-workspace.py doctor --serial <jlink-serial> --json
python3 Tools/firmware-workspace.py import-images --input <request.firmware-import.json> --json
python3 Tools/firmware-workspace.py resolve --selection .vscode/active-selection.json --operation build --json
python3 Tools/firmware-workspace.py build --selection .vscode/active-selection.json --json
python3 Tools/firmware-workspace.py build --selection .vscode/active-selection.json --clean --json
python3 Tools/firmware-workspace.py load --selection .vscode/active-selection.json --receipt <receipt.json> --serial <jlink-serial> --json
# Explicit recovery after diagnosis; ordinary retry is blocked.
python3 Tools/firmware-workspace.py load --selection .vscode/active-selection.json --receipt <receipt.json> --serial <jlink-serial> --recover --json
python3 Tools/firmware-workspace.py debug-config --selection .vscode/active-selection.json --receipt <receipt.json> --core cr8_0 --serial <jlink-serial> --json
python3 Tools/firmware-workspace.py console --selection .vscode/active-selection.json --receipt <receipt.json> --core cr8_0 --serial <jlink-serial> --action start --json
python3 Tools/firmware-workspace.py console --selection .vscode/active-selection.json --receipt <receipt.json> --serial <jlink-serial> --action stop --json
```

`resolve --operation` accepts build, load, debug or console; defaults to build. Load/debug capabilities do not gate build-only profiles.
`--clean` changes one build invocation without rewriting the saved selection. Target-switch cleanup remains owned by the original build scripts.
`probe-session --serial <serial> --json` reserves a physical probe while stdin remains open; its first line returns a leaseToken and serial. Editor child operations inherit `FIRMWARE_PROBE_LEASE` and `FIRMWARE_PROBE_SERIAL`. It performs no target connection itself. Closing stdin stops its owned console and releases the reservation after child teardown.

## Contracts

- Selection (`firmware-selection.schema.json`): schemaVersion, id, board, core, build.{family,target|config,mode}; groups use group plus build.{family,mode}; optional load.{recipe}, debug.{mode}.
- Receipt (`artifact-receipt.schema.json`): receiptId, timestamp, family, board, core, selectionId, target/config/group, gitRevision/gitDirty, compiler, artifacts[{path,sha256,size,core,entryPoint,rttAddress}], status; group receipts also bind groupDefinitionSha256.
- Import (`firmware-import.schema.json`): schemaVersion 1, UUID requestId, embedded selection and one/two core-keyed sources. File/folder sources require an exact member declaration; folder requires an explicitly chosen relativePath. Receipt sources select artifactCore from a build-receipt or managed prepared-receipt. Duplicate JSON keys and folder symlink escapes fail admission.
- Builders retain receipt v1. Imports emit v2 with operation import-images, requestId, nullable Git/compiler fields, per-artifact provenance/sourceObservation/member/checks. Evidence is receipt-reported, developer-declared or unknown and never upgrades on reimport. A single captured image is provisional and unloadable; both admitted members publish a committed pair. Completed captures and atomic preparation manifests support exact-request resume after interruption.
- Exact-request replay preserves recorded optional ELF metadata across symbol-tool changes; use a new preparation to refresh it. Startup admission rejects known M-profile/non-ARM ISA attributes when mapping symbols are absent, while allowing ARM starts with Thumb helpers. Pair-state reads, generation/request guards, persistence and publication share one queue; stale validation/history cannot replace newer assignments, and target transitions wait for pending pair saves.
- Result (`operation-result.schema.json`): protocolVersion, operationId, status, data, diagnostics[{level,code,message,path}], childExitCode, receiptPath.
- Exit codes: 0 success, 1 execution failure, 2 invalid input/admission, 3 blocked/recovery required, 130 cancelled. Status is ok, failed, blocked or cancelled; exit codes and status are distinct fields.
- Committed receipts must match the exact selection and image set. Load uses private rehashed copies and canonical exact-device/hash admission. Debug symbols use a retained immutable snapshot. Receipt origin is reported metadata, never independent build attestation or hardware qualification.
- Catalog capabilities advertise importImages, receiptVersions, preparedIdentity, strictLoadedIdentity, progressEvents and targetHistory. New actions check their required versions without blocking legacy commands. Import prerequisites are Python/jsonschema and arm-none-eabi-readelf; compiler/build tools/probes are operation-specific.
- Prepared load/debug optionally require --expect-receipt-id and --expect-pair-sha256 before probe access. --require-loaded is opt-in for debug-config; the new view uses it, legacy callers retain their default. Pair digest is SHA-256 of compact UTF-8 JSON [boardId,groupId,groupDefinitionSha256,[["cr8_0",hash0],["cr8_1",hash1]]]. Receipt ID is excluded from byte identity.
- Doctor --serial reads host-only journal history, without creating a runtime directory. Last load verified is historical. Incomplete legacy/failure journal writes invalidate verified pair identity. Load progress is prefixed PX4_WORKSPACE_EVENT JSON on stderr; stdout remains one terminal OperationResult. Operation UUID, actual per-core steps and private operation log paths bind results.

## Boundaries

Restricted Mode runs no repository code and writes no workspace files. Settings and state belong to the selected workspace folder; never assume folder zero.
Build tasks, root make, root build.sh and standalone/dual builders share a live inherited flock through staging.
The Firmware Setup view stores named variants of existing fixed RDK CR8 groups; it does not author new groups. Per-core Build preserves the peer capture; Build All adopts its returned receipt; Build & Load uses only its own adopted pair; Load never builds implicitly. Canonical local v2 setup state is separate from the derived legacy projection.
Managed consoles provide interactive RTT and R8-0 SCI4 on the fixed SCI4/RTT setup. SCI4 requires Linux-host picocom, configured Python and a local character-device path; it takes a UART kernel lock without J-Link. One RTT/debug owner remains allowed; SCI4 may coexist with peer RTT. Stop Sessions cleans only exact owned sessions, and switching inputs requires stopped sessions. Other UART routes retain `nsh_console_exec.py --serial <device>`. The physical J-Link serial is passed as JLINK_SERIAL to the RTT bridge, never as a positional core argument.
Only guarded RZ/V2H CR8 RAM loading is managed. Persistent flash and direct RZ/V2H CM33 connect are blocked. RA loading remains gated. Build compatibility is separate from hardware qualification.
Per-probe/core target state lives in a private user runtime directory. Started/interrupted or failed operations require explicit recovery; never erase the journal to bypass admission.
Cortex-Debug configurations are resolved in memory. Managed configurations use an owned server wrapper so supervisor cleanup covers the actual J-Link server after adapter/extension failure. The extension preserves launch.json and unrelated sessions/processes. Existing CMake-generated launch.generated.json remains a candidate, not an extension-managed launch entry.

SCI4 supervisor (internal, no target connection): `PYTHONPATH=Tools python3 -m firmware_workspace.serial_console --device <host-uart> --baud 115200 --session-id <UUID>`. It launches only the existing interactive helper, preserves terminal stdio, and passes its kernel lock through exec. Exit 4 = UART_BUSY, 2 = prerequisites, 1 = client failure, 130 = cancelled, 0 = normal. `--check` checks kernel lease availability without starting a client; metadata is observation-only. Never kill a persisted PID to bypass ownership. Real picocom/native VS Code and board acceptance remain separate from host fixture tests.
